### apng/encoder.js
Size-optimising animated PNG encoder. RGBA8 frames in, one .apng file out.
Pure logic — no DOM — so it runs unchanged in a Worker, which is where it
belongs (see apng/worker.js).

Exports: encodeApng, deflateZlib, delayFraction
Types: ApngFrame, ApngOptions, ApngResult, ApngFrameStat, ApngEffort,
  ApngColorType, Deflate

  const result = await encodeApng(width, height, frames, { threshold: 2 });
  // result.bytes is the file; result.frames explains what it did per frame.

encodeApng(width, height, frames, options?) -> Promise<ApngResult>
  frames: { data: Uint8Array | Uint8ClampedArray, delayMs?: number }[]
  Every frame must be exactly width*height*4 bytes of non-premultiplied RGBA8.
  Throws on a wrong-sized frame, a non-positive size, or an empty list.

What it does beyond writing the frames out, all of it aimed at file size:
  - DIRTY RECTANGLES: each frame stores only the bounding box of the pixels
    that moved since the previous one.
  - TRANSPARENT SKIPPING: inside that box, pixels that did not move are
    written fully transparent and composited with blend_op=OVER, so the
    decoder keeps what was there and deflate sees long runs of one value.
    Only legal when every changed pixel is opaque (OVER reproduces its source
    exactly only at alpha 255) — otherwise the frame falls back to SOURCE.
  - THRESHOLD: a channel movement of `threshold` or less is not a movement.
    Default 2 — invisible at 8 bits, and enough to absorb the +-1 noise that
    otherwise leaves a dirty-rect encoder with nothing static to find. 0 is
    exact/lossless. Comparison is against the CANVAS A DECODER WOULD SHOW, not
    the previous source frame, so tolerated differences cannot accumulate:
    every output pixel stays within `threshold` of its source, forever.
  - COALESCING: a frame that changes nothing is dropped and its delay added to
    the frame before it (`coalesce`, default true).
  - EXACT PALETTE: <= 256 distinct RGBA values become an 8-bit indexed PNG,
    one byte per pixel instead of four. Detection is exact and never
    quantises; `colorType: 'indexed'` on frames that do not fit throws rather
    than approximating.
  - FILTERING: per-row adaptive filter selection by default; `effort: 'best'`
    compresses every legal (blend op, filter strategy) pairing per frame and
    keeps the smallest, at the cost of up to 12 deflate passes per frame.

ApngOptions: threshold=2, alphaThreshold=threshold, delayMs=100, loops=0
  (0 = forever), colorType='auto'|'rgba'|'indexed', filter (see apng/png.js),
  effort='fast'|'best', coalesce=true, deflate, onProgress(done, total).

ApngResult: bytes, width, height, frameCount (frames in the output),
  sourceFrameCount, colorType ('rgba'|'indexed'), paletteSize, frames
  (ApngFrameStat[]: index, sourceIndex, rect, blend, filter, bytes, changed,
  delayMs, coalesced) — enough to show a per-frame size/rect breakdown.

deflateZlib(bytes) -> Promise<Uint8Array> is the default compressor,
`CompressionStream('deflate')`. Pass `options.deflate` to swap in a slower,
denser one; the encoder only requires a zlib stream back.

delayFraction(ms) -> { num, den } is APNG's uint16 delay fraction, exported
because a caller reading back an fcTL needs the same rounding.

### apng/worker.js
Running apng/encoder.js off the main thread: the worker-side handler and the
main-thread client. DOM/Worker-bound, so it is not node-tested.

Exports: installApngWorker, createApngEncoder
Types: ApngEncoder, ApngWorkerOptions, ApngProgress, ApngEncodeRequest,
  ApngWorkerResponse

A worker script must be same-origin, so the consumer owns a two-line worker
file and this module supplies the body:

  // apng-worker.js, served from the consumer's own origin
  import { installApngWorker } from 'https://…/apng/worker.js';
  installApngWorker();

  // main thread
  const encoder = createApngEncoder(new URL('./apng-worker.js', import.meta.url));
  const result = await encoder.encode(w, h, frames, { threshold: 2 }, onProgress);

installApngWorker() registers the message handler on the current worker
global. It THROWS if that global has a `document` — encoding on the main
thread is the thing this module exists to prevent, so there is no in-page
fallback anywhere in it.

createApngEncoder(workerUrl, { transferFrames = false }) -> ApngEncoder
  .encode(width, height, frames, options?, onProgress?) -> Promise<ApngResult>
  .terminate()  kill the worker, rejecting everything in flight; the next
                encode spawns a fresh one (this is how you abandon a long
                encode whose inputs just changed)

FRAMES MAY BE BITMAPS: each entry is either `{ data, delayMs? }` (RGBA8
already at the output size) or `{ bitmap, delayMs? }` (an ImageBitmap of any
size, which the WORKER rasterises with apng/raster.js). Pass bitmaps and the
page never touches a pixel — decode a file with createImageBitmap, hand it
over, and both the scaling and the encoding happen off-thread.
`options.fit` ('contain' default | 'cover' | 'stretch') places a bitmap whose
aspect ratio differs from the output's; 'contain' leaves the bars transparent,
which an APNG stores for almost nothing.

`options` is otherwise ApngOptions minus its function fields (they cannot be
cloned); progress arrives through the `onProgress` argument instead.
`transferFrames` moves the frame BYTE buffers into the worker rather than
copying them — faster and half the peak memory, but it detaches the caller's
arrays. Bitmaps are never transferred, since a caller that re-encodes when a
setting changes still needs them.

### apng/raster.js
Fitting and drawing a source into an RGBA8 frame. The maths is pure and
node-tested; only rasterizeToRgba needs a canvas (OffscreenCanvas, so it runs
in a worker).

Exports: fitRect, clampSize, rasterizeToRgba
Types: FitMode = 'contain'|'cover'|'stretch', FitRect { x, y, w, h }

- fitRect(srcW, srcH, dstW, dstH, mode='contain') -> FitRect — where to draw a
  source inside a differently-shaped canvas. 'contain' fits it whole and
  centres it, 'cover' fills and overflows, 'stretch' ignores aspect ratio.
  Throws on a non-positive source size.
- clampSize(width, height, max) -> { width, height } — scale down so neither
  side exceeds `max`, keeping the ratio, never scaling up, never returning 0.
- rasterizeToRgba(source, width, height, mode='contain') -> Uint8ClampedArray
  — draw any CanvasImageSource into a fresh transparent canvas of that size.
  Throws where OffscreenCanvas does not exist rather than returning blanks.

### apng/png.js
PNG container primitives: CRC-32, chunk framing, scanline filtering. Pure.

Exports: PNG_SIGNATURE, crc32, writeChunk, concatBytes, paeth,
  filterScanlines, unfilterScanlines, FILTER_STRATEGIES
Type: FilterStrategy = 'none'|'sub'|'up'|'average'|'paeth'|'adaptive'

- crc32(bytes, seed=0) — the zlib polynomial; `seed` continues a running CRC
  (pass a previous finalised value) so a chunk's type and data can be fed in
  separately.
- writeChunk(type, data) — length + 4-char type + data + CRC. Throws unless
  `type` is exactly 4 characters.
- filterScanlines(raw, stride, height, bpp, strategy='adaptive') — PNG's
  pre-compression form: one filter byte then `stride` residual bytes per row.
  `bpp` is the byte distance to the pixel on the left (4 for RGBA8, 1 for
  8-bit indexed). 'adaptive' is the standard minimum-sum-of-absolute-
  differences choice per row.
- unfilterScanlines(filtered, stride, height, bpp) — the inverse, for a
  caller that verifies its own output or reads a PNG it did not write.
  Throws on an unknown filter type.

### apng/diff.js
Inter-frame differencing: which pixels moved, the box around them, and the
two ways to encode it. Pure.

Exports: diffFrames, cropRect, cropRectMasked, composite
Types: Rect { x, y, w, h }, FrameDiff { rect, changed, opaque }, DiffOptions
  { threshold?, alphaThreshold? }

- diffFrames(canvas, next, width, height, options?) -> FrameDiff | null
  null means nothing changed past the threshold. `opaque` reports whether
  every changed pixel is fully opaque, which is exactly when the OVER
  encoding is legal.
- cropRect(src, width, rect) — copy the rectangle out verbatim (the SOURCE
  payload).
- cropRectMasked(canvas, next, width, rect, options?, fill=[0,0,0,0]) — the
  same crop with unchanged pixels replaced by a transparent pixel (the OVER
  payload). An indexed encoder must pass its transparent palette entry's
  colour as `fill`: any alpha-0 colour is equally invisible, but only the one
  in the palette can be stored.
- composite(canvas, width, rect, payload, blend) — advance a canvas the way a
  decoder would ('source' replaces the rectangle, 'over' skips transparent
  pixels). This is the encoder's model of the screen; it is also what a
  consumer needs to replay an APNG it decoded.

### apng/palette.js
Exact palette detection for 8-bit indexed output. Pure.

Exports: buildPalette, indexImage, packRgba
Type: Palette { rgba, size, trnsCount, transparentIndex, lookup }

- buildPalette(images, limit=256, reserveTransparent=true) -> Palette | null
  null when the images use more than the budget of distinct RGBA values. It
  bails as soon as the count is exceeded, so photographic input costs a few
  thousand pixel reads rather than a full scan. NOTHING HERE QUANTISES:
  indexing can never change a pixel. Entries are ordered non-opaque first, so
  the tRNS chunk (a prefix of the palette) is as short as possible, then most-
  used first. `reserveTransparent` guarantees a fully transparent entry for
  masked frames, which costs one slot — so fully opaque input fits 255
  colours, not 256.
- indexImage(src, palette) -> Uint8Array, one byte per pixel. Throws on a
  colour the palette lacks rather than substituting a near one.
- packRgba(r, g, b, a) -> number, the endian-independent lookup key.
